recipes.name: Rachael’s Superheated Cajun Boiled Peanuts
ingredients_raw: 1 (3 ounce) package dry crab boil (such as Zatarain's® Crab and Shrimp Boil)

steps.text: Place peanuts, salt, jalapeños, red pepper flakes, crab boil, Cajun seasoning, and garlic powder into a slow cooker. Pour in water to cover the peanuts and stir to combine. Cover and cook on Low until peanuts are soft, at least 24 hours. Stir occasionally and add water as needed to keep the peanuts covered. Drain, then serve hot or cold.

raw_recipe.headline: Rachael’s Superheated Cajun Boiled Peanuts
raw_recipe.description: Slow-cooked peanuts are boiled with Cajun seasoning, crab boil, pepper flakes, and jalapeños, resulting in a zesty snack found in the heart of Florida.

review.reviewBody: Hi, this is Rachael. I read some of the recent reviews and I feel that's it's unfair to poorly rate this recipe if you don't like the consistentcy of boiled peanuts! This isn't to make crunchy, roasted peanuts, its for soft, boiled peanuts! For the rest of you, I am so THRILLED that ya'll have enjoyed this recipe!

I'm on board with Rachael (submitter of recipe)...if you don't know what "boiled peanuts" are all about, then don't submit a bad rating due to texture issues! I'm a northerner but have lived in the south and got hooked on these. I like this flavor way better then just plain salted ones. I used organic dry raw peanuts (2lbs) cuz when I got my craving, green peanuts weren't in season. I soaked my peanuts overnight in cold water (weighed em down w/a plate) drained, then proceeded with the recipe. I didn't use 'crab boil' - added some Old Bay. I also added a bottle of Honey Brown Ale initially and cooked in a 8QT heavy stock pot on the stove. If you store the pot in the fridge overnight (after cooking for 12 hrs) the peanuts tend to suck up more liquid and will finally sink down; then continue cooking next day. You have to sample one here n there until you get the texture you prefer. If you don't use green peanuts you may have to cook longer. If I had a pressure cooker I would try method mentioned. All I can say is if you want crunchy peanuts, don't try these or rate poorly because these are meant to be softish (like canned kidney beans). I like mine soft, but that's a personal pref. In any case, love the additional spice profile!

I made these last night. I started them at 10pm and by 10am they were done. I used my 6 quart crock pot for a pound and a half of nuts and a gallon of water. I followed the directions and I added extra of the spices and jalapeno peppers for more heat. I checked the water after a 1/4 cup salt and it was salty enough for me, as I am watching my sodium intake and I love salt. The water was extra spicy and burned my mouth in a good way. The nuts have a nice flavor, but not hot and spicy at all. I also used GREEN PEANUTS. Will make these again.

We absolutely LOVE this recipe! The only problem was that we didn't cook enough and are making another batch now. We made a few changes….we left out the jalapeños, added some cayenne pepper, used 1/4 cup regular salt and 1/4 cup sea salt, and instead of regular crab boil I used Old Bay Blackened seasoning and some regular Old Bay. I let them soak in the seasoned water for about 3 hours before I put them in the crock pot. Also, it took about 36 hours to cook in our crock pot, not 24. They turned out incredible! Thanks for sharing!!

I think this recipe would prob be perfect as written if you like heat. I omitted the jalapeño, salt, garlic powder and red pepper just to keep it simpler (I prefer unsalted nuts in general). I used liquid boil (following the instructions on the package). This recipe was an excellent starting point. I was afraid to keep the slow cooker on overnight so they cooked for about 15 hours on low and then stayed in the brine in the fridge overnight. Perfect for me.

Backed off the salt a tad due to the Cajun seasoning that is salty and the crab boil. Added 1-1/2 cup of sliced dill pickle with the brine. I like spicy so I add cayenne pepper and also more red pepper flake and jalapeno to mine.. the secret if you cook boiled peanuts as much as me is PRESSURE COOKER!!!!! They are done and perfect in 4 hours. Crock pot is normally 24 hrs. ENJOY!!!

While the flavor was good, I, and the friends I had try this, thought it was much too salty. I followed the recipe exactly. I've let it sit on warm in the crockpot after the 1 day of cooking on low and added more and more water to try to dilute it, it has made it a little better (i.e. less salty). 

Next batch, I'll cut the salt down by at least half. Don't think 1/2 cup salt is needed/should be used. Typo on the recipe or just large difference in saltiness preference?

Guarantee all the people complaining about the salt is because of their cajun seasoning. You gotta check the ingredients. I always use cajun seasoning that doesn't have any salt in it. BUT if you look at the ingredients list on most cajun seasonings, salt is the first thing listed, which means it's the most abundant. Gotta make sure you get salt-free cajun seasoning, I.E. blackening seasoning.
I love this recipe! I’ve recently converted it from my slow cooker to my pressure cooker. Now I can have my peanuts in about 2 hours vs. the slow cooker.

I love boiled peanuts. The recipe as written is more salty than I'd prefer. I've made it twice... once exactly as written, the second time I used more old bay and less salt. The time needed to be extended a lot too. The peanuts were too crunchy so I kept the slow cooker on overnight. Overall I'd make this recipe again. Thank you for sharing.

My daughter asked me to make these for her and she really liked them, but said to use less salt. I told her other people said the same thing, so next time I will use only half and go from there. You can always add, but not take away. Just a warning, your whole house will smell like boiled peanuts when they are cooking. It might be a bit much for those with allergies. I thought about putting my slow cooker in the garage due to the scent. We used a 24 ounce bag of raw peanuts and adjusted the ingredients. The peanuts will float at first, so you have to stir them often until they start taking on some water, which sinks them a bit. Once that happens, you don't really have to stir it. I gave this a 4 star rating due to the salt.
Absolutely yummy! Thank you for sharing. Will make again and again!

This recipe is one of the easiest boiled peanut recipes ever, which is nice however for those who keep complaining about the salt when I was reading the recipe, I automatically knew I don’t like my food too salty so I cut back on it by reading the recipe, I knew that it was too much for me. Everyone has preferences. Also, I didn’t add a crab boil seasoning instead I made my own crab boil seasoning and put it in. So have fun with the recipe, add to it take away from it. Do what you feel is comfortable for your family and your tastebuds, but the recipe itself is a great recipe.
Wayyyyyy too salty!!! We couldn't even eat them!
I didn't think it was too salty as others suggested, I kept my water level topped off though. These did stink up the house as some others noted though. Next time I'll cook outside!

Mine are still in the crockpot. Just had a taste after 10 hours. Way too salty. I would cut the salt back to 1/4 cup. I’m adding more water to help with the saltiness. I’m not sure if they are going to be edible. Time will tell.
yes, check the water level, especially in the middle of the night! for some reason

Greatful for the recipe, I'm from Eustis Fl, just on the south end of Ocala National Forest, I miss ole man Roy's peanuts, he used to set up near Buck&Does corner store, please add whole new potatoes and pickle slices as they are missing from the recipe.

Craving roadside boiled peanuts I find in the South but living in Brooklyn, I needed to find a recipe that could replicate that deliciousness. This is it. This recipe is the closest I have come to getting that roadside, Georgia flavor. I cut the salt and don't always add the jalapeño and the peanuts always turn out amazing and especially addictive.

Signed up for this dumb site and risked an inbox full of spam emails just to leave a review. Been a Floridian in California for 15 years, but these were an instant teleportation device. So. Good. Perfect recipe. Did 10 hours on low and 10 hours on high in the crock pot. Football! Fall! Bowlt peanuts! Yay.
